newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to chair Palestinian national dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to chair Palestinian national dialogue.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will chair on Thursday the first national unity dialogue in five years grouping Palestinian Islamic and secular factions, PLO officials said on Monday.

The conference will discuss the PLO's talks with Israel on a permanent peace settlement and relations between the Palestinian Authority and opponents of Arafat's peace deals with the Jewish state, they said.

The officials said all factions belonging to the Palestine Liberation Organisation would attend the meeting in the West Bank city of Nablus. Opposition groups, such as the militant Islamic movement Hamas, that are not PLO members also would be there.

It will be the first broad national dialogue since Hamas and the PLO met in late 1992 for three days in Tunis to discuss Israel's deportation to south Lebanon of more than 400 Hamas and Islamic Jihad activists.
The PLO's 11 factions, six of which oppose the self-rule deals with Israel, last convened in April in Gaza.

"We invited all factions to participate in the dialogue. All said they would attend except for the Islamic Jihad group. The dialogue will have an open agenda because the Authority doesn't want to impose one on any faction," Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general secretary of the Palestinian Presidency, told Reuters.

Arafat called for a national unity dialogue last September to unite opposition to what Palestinians charge is mounting Israeli confiscation of Arab land in Gaza and the West Bank, including occupied East Jerusalem, to expand Jewish settlements.

Opposition leaders said there was a national consensus among Palestinians that final-status talks with Israel, due to resume in March, should result in an independent Palestinian state in the West Bank and Gaza with East Jerusalem as its capital.
But the PLO factions are divided over launching military attacks against Israel.

Two Damascus-based PLO factions, the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine and the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, favour armed struggle. Hamas and Islamic Jihad also advocate armed resistance to Israeli occupation.

Opposition leaders said they doubted the dialogue would bridge gaps between the Authority and their factions since Arafat was constrained by his peace deals with Israel and because he dominated Palestinian politics.

A Hamas leaflet issued on Monday said "despite suspicion of the seriousness of reaching concrete results...the movement's leadership considers that national interest necessitates accepting this invitation".
Hamas officials said they were worried if they boycotted Thursday's meeting, they would be isolated politically and their improving relations with the Authority would deteriorate.

Hamas said it hopes "the dialogue would result in renouncing violence in settling political disputes and to unite Palestinians against Israeli aggression by using all means including the peoples' right to military resistance against occupation everywhere".

Palestinian police cracked down on Hamas, nearly destroying its infrastructure, last year after a wave of Hamas suicide bombings killed scores of people in Israel. Several PLO-Hamas reconciliation attempts failed after Hamas rejected Arafat's demand to stop military activities.
The PLO insists opposition groups must respect the Authority's peace deals with Israel.

Islamic Jihad group said in a leaflet it would boycott the national dialogue. The movement called for Palestinian unity against what it called Israeli aggression on Palestinian land and rights and urged PLO-Israeli talks be halted.
